title: Machine-learning screening identifies bacterial-selective membrane-active compounds
summary: The June 2026 bioRxiv version describes an initial machine-learning-guided screen of ZINC20 compounds balancing predicted antibacterial activity, mammalian-cell toxicity, and mechanism-of-action novelty. Among 61 purchased candidates, six showed partial growth inhibition; 49 were non-toxic to HepG2 cells at 50 μM. Flow cytometry indicated membrane disruption for four of the six initial active hits and membrane depolarization for two. A September version reports additional screening and revised models; its expanded results are not attributed to the June version here. The study does not report a novel protein target or clinical antibiotic.
ai_technology: Graph-convolutional neural networks for antibacterial activity/toxicity with XGBoost mechanism-of-action classification and novelty filtering

evidence.tested: The June 2026 v1 reports that 61 purchased candidates were tested, six showed partial growth inhibition, and 49/61 were non-toxic to HepG2 cells at 50 μM. Flow cytometry indicated membrane integrity disruption for four initial active hits and membrane depolarization for two.
evidence.unknown: The initial work does not report a novel protein target and is limited to the stated bacterial assays and HepG2 toxicity concentration. The September version adds expanded screening and revised analyses; those later results are not attributed to the June v1.
evidence.ai_role: Learned activity and toxicity models, together with a mechanism-novelty classifier, prioritized compounds for purchase and experimental testing.

source_review.scope: Primary PMC-indexed full text for the June bioRxiv v1, primary PubMed preprint abstract/metadata, and primary PMC/PubMed metadata for the later September version to distinguish version-specific results.
